dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise.
Good morning. Pardon me, is this the right number for a tree? I wasn't sure, because I know City Hall isn't open on a Sunday.
You've got the right place. The storm line is staffed this weekend for exactly that. What's going on with the tree?

Well, a whole tree came down across the side street next to my house. The whole thing, root ball and all, just laid over right across the road. It happened last night, in the worst of the wind. Pardon me, can you hear me all right?
I hear you fine. Take your time. Whole tree across the street, nobody hurt?

No, no, nobody hurt. Nobody was out. But a car can't get by, and it's one of those narrow streets. I looked this morning and it's just sitting there. Honestly I'm a little irritated, I've been trying to work out who to even call since seven.
Okay, let me get a few things. What's the street, and where on it?
I'm at 458 Gibbs Avenue, on the Ocean Drive side. The tree is on the little side street right by my property line. It's blocking the whole width.
Pardon me one moment. Sweetheart, no, not at the phone. She is waving her stuffed rabbit at the receiver. My granddaughter, she is two and she wants the rabbit to talk to you.
Well, tell the rabbit good morning from me. Is that rabbit going to be okay out there in this weather?

Oh, he's staying inside, thank you. Pardon me. So, my real question is who handles this. Is it the city, or is it whoever owns the tree, or the electric company? I don't know whose job it is and nobody has told me.

Good question, and it depends. If the tree is on a city street or city property, or it's in the road right-of-way, Public Works deals with clearing the road. If it's on private property, the removal of the tree itself is usually the owner's responsibility, though we'd still open the road if it's blocked. And if it's pulled down wires, that's the utility and you stay well away.
I see. Pardon me, I didn't see any wires on the ground. I looked from the window. There's a line up high that goes to the pole, and I can't tell if the tree is touching it.
Then I'll note possible contact with a line, and I'd ask you to keep everybody back from it. Don't go out and try to move anything. Is the tree leaning on the wire, or just near it?
Near it, I think. It's hard to tell. The branches are all tangled up at the top.
That's fine, I'll write it that way. Do you know whose yard it came out of? Is it a neighbor's, or does it look like it was on the street edge?
It came out of the empty lot across from me. Nobody lives there. I believe the owner is somebody out of state, but I couldn't tell you the name.

Alright. That makes it a bit of a gray area, but the road being blocked is what moves it up. We'll send a crew to clear the travel lane. Whether they cut it all up and haul it away, that may be a separate matter with the owner.
Pardon me, so the city will come? Even today? It is Sunday, and the storm only finished this morning.

The crews are out now, and they're working through a list. Blocked roads and anything touching wires go first. Yours is a blocked road, so it's near the top. I'd say plan on sometime today or into tomorrow morning.
Alright. I would just like it written down that I called early. I've called a couple of other numbers this morning and got a machine.
It's written. Time of call is just before nine. Now, the tree has a name for the crew, so let me ask: is the street name posted? What does the sign say at the corner?

Pardon me, let me look. I can see it from the front window. Hold on. [pause] Yes, I'm back. I can't read it from here, the sign is turned. I'd say it's the little street that runs down toward the water off Gibbs.
That's enough. With your address and that description, they'll find it. Is there anything in the road besides the tree, like debris or a car that's stuck?
No car. Just a lot of branches, and some shingles from somewhere. The rabbit says thank you, by the way.
You tell the rabbit he's welcome. Can I get a number in case the crew needs to reach you at the house?
Yes, it's 401-555-0180. That is the house phone. I'll be here all day.
Got it, 401-555-0180. And it's Mr. Duarte?
Yes, Nilson Duarte. Pardon me, D-U-A-R-T-E, people always put an extra letter in.
D-U-A-R-T-E. Perfect. So here's what I have: downed tree fully across the side street off Gibbs Avenue near 458, from the empty lot across, possible contact with an overhead line, no injuries.
That's right. Pardon me, one more thing. If the electric company needs to come first, who calls them? Do I call, or do you?
I'd go ahead and call them yourself, since you can see the line. Tell them there's a tree on a line and give your address. I'll also flag it on our side so the crew checks before they cut.
Alright, I'll do that. And for next time, God forbid, is this the number to use for any tree that comes down?

For anything in the street or on city property, yes, this line during the storm, and the regular Public Works number on weekdays. If it's down in someone's own yard and not blocking anything, that's generally between you and a tree service.
I understand. Thank you. I only wish somebody had said so at seven o'clock.
Fair enough. Sorry for the runaround. Keep that road clear of kids and the rabbit, and the crew will get there as soon as they can.
I will. Thank you, Miss Arruda. Pardon me, good day to you.
You too, Mr. Duarte. Bye now.
